Plugins

Self-contained packages of codepoints above the Base ceiling.

A plugin is a self-contained package of codepoints: it declares ranges (all strictly above 0x7FFFFFFF), a name table, properties, mappings and optional collation. A plugin blob is a single packed file validated before it is ever mounted.

Lifecycle

  1. Install & stage. The blob lands in the staging table. The API returns SUCS_PLUGIN_REBOOT_REQUIRED (status 13).
  2. Reboot. Mandatory — mounting changes the active namespace, exactly like switching a runtime mode.
  3. Boot commit. plugin_commit_on_boot() verifies CRC32c + Fletcher-64, then validates ranges (sorted, non-overlapping, above the base limit, no collisions with mounted plugins).
  4. Mount. A valid plugin mounts as a SuperUnicode Plugin Partition — OWFS exclusively, read-only.
  5. Register. The plugin’s ranges enter the active ExtSUCS namespace and codepoint lookups can resolve them.
  6. Quarantine. Any failed gate quarantines the plugin; it is never mounted and never registers.

Blob format

The blob header (94 bytes, packed) carries the magic SUCS, blob version, the plugin version (major.minor.patch), the plugin id (64 bytes), range count, blob size, and the two integrity checksums computed over the whole blob with the checksum fields zeroed.

magic "SUCS" | blob_version 1 | ver major.minor.patch | id[64]
| range_count | blob_size | crc32c | fletcher64
then ranges (16-byte LE pairs), then the payload

Practical guide: the plugin SDK, and the plugin sources in the repository.
